reasons: Rule applies correctly: Section 3.4 is an inspection right running against the Company (our client, the customer) over its payment-calculation records, so the AUDIT rule is engaged.

Deviation classification is sound: the clause contains no frequency cap at all, and unlimited audits fall below the fallback (once per year) and into the rule's walk-away territory, so this is a material term failure rather than a minor sub-element.

Redline is the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position — a single inserted 'no more than once in any twelve (12) month period' phrase, leaving the already-acceptable 30-day notice, business-hours limitation and HDI-borne cost untouched; grammar remains clean.

No system-access language exists to delete (inspection is limited to records held by the Company's General Manager), and the rationale correctly notes the non-independent inspector and absent underpayment shift-back as observations rather than separate flags.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required first-person-plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix, and correctly states what changed and why; deterministic checks are consistent and the advisory changed-character ratio reflects diff granularity, not an over-broad rewrite.
